review.tagline: Vectorless RAG that builds a tree index of a PDF and lets an LLM search it
review.summary: PageIndex builds a hierarchical tree index from each PDF, then has an LLM reason through that tree to find the relevant sections, with no vector database or chunking. The Python SDK (pip install pageindex) runs locally with your own LLM key for text-based PDFs, or points at PageIndex Cloud for OCR, scanned documents and block-level citations. The README reports 98.7% on FinanceBench and about $0.001 per page to index locally.
review.audience: Developers building document Q&A over long PDFs such as filings and manuals
strengths: No vector DB or chunking; retrieval is traceable to page-level references
Local mode indexes a 1,000-page PDF for roughly a dollar, per README benchmarks
Same client switches between local and Cloud by changing the index argument
Documents integration with OpenAI Agents SDK and Claude Agent SDK
weaknesses: Local mode handles text-based PDFs only; no OCR or image understanding
MCP server, metadata, folders and File System for large corpora are Cloud-only
Each query needs LLM reasoning calls, so accuracy and cost depend on the chat model
Needs an external LLM API key; local-model support is not stated in the README
needs: Needs LLM API key (e.g. OpenAI), PageIndex API key (Cloud mode only)
Models: OpenAI models (gpt series), other providers configurable per docs
